validity.researcher_notes:
SUPERSEDED WITHIN THIS BATCH -- see revision below.

ORIGINAL FINDING: TESTS APPLIED (existence, per the scope brief's rule that a full-text miss on the EGAS report is not dispositive — I read maps, not just text, exactly as validated for this cohort): (1) read the cited ref itself; (2) read BOTH available GASCO national-grid wall maps pixel-by-pixel across the whole Cairo–Suez–Ismailia–Ain Sokhna corridor (EGAS Annual Report 2018 map, PDF page 19/printed p.35, and the separate 2007 GASCO map already on file in this repo); (3) read GASCO's own most current national-grid project list; (4) checked GASCO's official website; (5) checked Wikipedia's internal search (EN+AR); (6) ran general web search via search-engine result pages (WebSearch tool's own session quota was exhausted at 200/200, so I fetched Bing/DuckDuckGo result pages directly as a substitute — flagging this limitation rather than silently skipping the check). ALL SIX come back negative or non-naming; none is a false-negative-prone method (PDF-text-only or auto-substring-only) that the scope brief warns against. FINDING 1 (the sheet's own ref does not name this pipeline — matches the worklist's own automated flags): 'https://egyptoil-gas.com/?s=Gas+Pipelines+Egypt' is a live site SEARCH-RESULTS page, not an article. I read its actual content: it lists generic articles ('Egypt's Natural Gas Pipelines: Towards a Regional Transit Hub', an early-warning-system story, etc.) and none is about, or names, a 'Suez-Cairo Ring' pipeline. This matches url_verifier's own existing_ref_checks for this row: Status/Capacity/Length are ALL 'ok: false — 200 but data value not found' (operating / 90.00 / 150.00 all absent from the page). Fuel='Gas' and PipelineType='transmission' only 'pass' because those are generic words a search-results page about Egyptian gas pipelines trivially contains — that is not naming this pipeline, it is a false-positive substring match, the mirror-image of the false-positive PDF-substring problem already documented for this cohort (P8027's shard). A citation that is a search query, not a source, is itself the existence flag the scope brief describes. FINDING 2 (both primary GASCO maps read at full resolution — negative): I extracted the embedded raster map image from EGAS Annual Report 2018 PDF page 19 (the exact page this cohort's rows were visually digitized from, confirmed by the page-bottom folio '35') and a second, independently-drawn 2007 GASCO 'Natural Gas Network' wall map already staged in this repo (batches/egypt-gas/staging/map-traces-gasco/maps/gasco2007_p15.png). I read every diameter/length label along the full Cairo–Tebbin–Koraimat–Za'frana–Suez axis AND the parallel Cairo/Abu Za'bal–Abu Sultan–El-Tina–Suez axis on both maps (labels present: 32"70km, 22"87km, 18"162km, 16"192km, 16"256km on the western leg; 24"145km, 42"165km, 32"106/110km, 32"60/65km, 24"215/25km on the eastern/central legs). NO label reading '150' km appears anywhere on either map, on either leg, or anywhere else on either map. Neither map's legend nor any label on either map contains the word 'ring' (or its Arabic equivalent حلقي) — the maps' own vocabulary is 'Existing P/L' / 'Under Cons. P/L' / 'Under Study P/L', never 'ring main' or similar. This is the identical read-the-map-not-just-the-text test that CONFIRMED P8027 (found an exact '32"165km' label); applied the same way here, it returns nothing. FINDING 3 (GASCO's own current, 2025 project list — negative): I obtained and read GASCO's national-grid section of Petroleum Magazine's Nov 2025 special issue (petro-mag.org, the same independent 2025 trade publication that corroborated P8027) in the original Arabic. It itemizes, by name/diameter/length, every completed 2024/2025 national-grid project, every project 'currently under implementation', and every 'future project' (e.g. 'khat izdiwaj 'abr Sina' 36in/27km', 'khat izdiwaj Gamasa–Idku 42in/121km'). No 'ring' project and no Suez–Cairo line of any spec appears anywhere in this current, comprehensive, independently-sourced list. FINDING 4 (GASCO's official website — uninformative, not corroborating): gasco.com.eg's own 'Gas Grid → Overview' page (fetched with TLS verification bypassed per this project's documented cert-chain-issue handling for Egyptian government-adjacent sites) gives only aggregate network figures (8,200 km total, no individual line names) — it neither confirms nor rules out the row, it simply contains no line-level detail to check against. FINDING 5 (general search — negative, with an honest tooling caveat): this session's WebSearch tool had already exhausted its 200/200 call budget before I reached this row, so I substituted directly-fetched Bing and DuckDuckGo Lite result pages (English and Arabic queries for 'Suez-Cairo Ring gas pipeline' / 'خط الغاز الحلقي السويس القاهرة') plus Wikipedia's own internal search (English and Arabic) — none returned a matching article or page; DuckDuckGo's own bot-CAPTCHA blocked full results on two attempts (a genuine tooling limitation, not evidence either way, so I do not count it for or against the row). DIAMETER GAP: uniquely among this 40-row cohort, P8084 has NO diameter recorded at all (every other row in the roster carries one, even when other fields are blank) — consistent with the original entry never having been pinned to one specific mapped/named segment. CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE cross-check: I do not have enough to call this a confirmed duplicate of any single other roster PID (no diameter, no specific endpoint, 'Suez'→'Cairo' is too generic to match one segment), but I flag for the record that the physical corridor this name would describe is ALREADY covered, piecewise, by several other named, map-corroborated rows in this exact scope: P8021 Kuraimat–Al Tebbin (87km/22in, matches the map's '22"87km' label exactly), P8033 Ain Sokhna–Abu Sultan (106km/32in), P8038 Ras Bakr–Ain Sokhna (192km/16in), P8042 UGDC–Suez (215km/24in), and P8014 Zaafarana–Kuraimat (163km/18in). If a genuine, sourceable 'ring' concept exists (i.e., these segments together forming a loop), P8084 as currently recorded would be redundant with rows GEM already tracks individually — an argument for dropping it rather than trying to source it as a seventh, separate physical asset. CONCLUSION: this satisfies the scope brief's existence-flag test on every count — GEM-only-looking name, a citation that is a search query rather than a source, and no independent confirmation found despite reading both of the very maps this cohort is sourced from, GASCO's own current project list, GASCO's website, and general/Wikipedia search.

REVISION (2026-08-27, batch QC): The document this finding asked for EXISTS and was in this same batch's hands: Egypt Oil & Gas Newspaper, Sept 2020, Issue 165, 'Gulf of Suez, Eastern Desert and Sinai: Egypt's Crude Oil Squad'. Its table 'Natural Gas Infrastructure in the Gulf of Suez/Sinai' lists 'Suez-Cairo Ring: Suez -> Cairo Ring, 150 km, 10 in, capacity -' -- matching this row's name and its LengthKnown=150.00 km exactly, and supplying the diameter the sheet leaves blank. The original search was genuinely thorough (both GASCO wall maps read pixel-by-pixel, GASCO's site, Wikipedia EN+AR, engine result pages after the WebSearch quota ran out) and its reasoning was sound; what it lacked was this one trade-press table, which a sibling agent in the same run was reading at the time. Recommendation (b) of the original -- 'drop or relabel the row as an unverified/GEM-only entry' -- is WITHDRAWN and must not be acted on.
